source_text:
Καὶ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἄλλων δὲ ἀνθρώπων ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθε, ἔστιν γὰρ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐλπὶς μετανοίας, ἵνα θεοῦ τύχωσιν. ἐπιτρέψατε οὖν αὐτοῖς κἂν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ὑμῖν μαθητευθῆναι.
πρὸς τὰς ὀργὰς αὐτῶν ὑμεῖς πραεῖς, πρὸς τὰς μεγαλορημοσύνας αὐτῶν ὑμεῖς ταπεινόφρονες, πρὸς τὰς βλασφημίας αὐτῶν ὑμεῖς τὰς προσευχάς, πρὸς τὴν πλάνην αὐτῶν αὐτῶν ὑμεῖς ἑδραῖοι τῇ πίστει, πρὸς τὸ ἄγριον αὐτῶν ὑμεῖς ἥμεροι, μῆ σπουδάζοντες ἀντιμιμήσασθαι αὐτούς,
ἀδελφοὶ αὐτῶν εὑρεθῶμεν τῇ ἐπιεικείᾳ: μιμηταὶ δὲ τοῦ κυρίου σπουδάζωμεν εἶναι, τίς πλέον ἀδικηθῇ, τίς ἀποστερηθῇ, τίς ἀθετηθῇ: ἵνα μὴ τοῦ διαβόλου βοτάνη τις εὑρεθῇ ἐν ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἐν πάσῃ ἁγνείᾳ καὶ σωφροσύνῃ μένητε ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ σαρκικῶς καὶ πνευματικῶς.
thought_title: Pray for others and answer evil with gentleness
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Ephesians, urging them to pray for outsiders and to respond to hostility with Christlike gentleness rather than imitation.
pass_a_gloss: And for the other people [also] pray without ceasing, for there is in them hope of repentance, so that they may obtain God. Allow therefore them at least from the works to be discipled by you. Toward their angers you [be] gentle, toward their boastful speeches you [be] humble-minded, toward their blasphemies you [offer] your prayers, toward their error [of] them you [be] steadfast in the faith, toward their wildness you [be] tame, not being eager to imitate them in return. [As] their brothers may we be found by gentleness; imitators of the Lord may we be eager to be, [asking] who may be wronged more, who may be defrauded, who may be rejected; so that no weed of the devil may be found among you, but in all purity and self-control may you remain in Jesus Christ fleshly and spiritually.

choices.why: Keeps the genitive as a simple possessive/qualifying genitive, matching the source's compactness.

choices.english: so that they may obtain God
choices.why: τυγχάνω with genitive means to attain or obtain; 'obtain God' preserves the striking directness of the Greek.
rejected: so that they may reach God
so that they may find God

choices.term: κἂν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ὑμῖν μαθητευθῆναι
choices.english: at least from the works to be discipled by you
choices.why: κἂν means 'at least' or 'even if only'; μαθητευθῆναι is passive, so 'be discipled by you' keeps the passive force and the dative agent.
rejected: to be taught by your deeds

choices.term: πρὸς τὰς ὀργὰς αὐτῶν ὑμεῖς πραεῖς
choices.why: The πρὸς + accusative construction sets up a contrast; keeping 'toward' preserves the parallel structure of the series.
rejected: in response to their anger, be gentle

choices.why: The ἀντι- prefix means 'in return' or 'in exchange'; rendering it explicitly preserves the reciprocal force.
In this negative context ('no weed of the devil'), 'weed' captures the agricultural metaphor of something unwanted growing among them.

pass_b_english: Pray without ceasing for other people as well, because there is hope of repentance in them, so that they may attain God. Allow them, then, to learn from you at least through your works.

Toward their outbursts of anger, be gentle. Toward their boasts, be humble-minded. Toward their blasphemies, offer prayers. Toward their error, stand steadfast in faith. Toward their savagery, be mild, not eager to imitate them in return.

Let us be found to be their brothers by our gentleness, and let us be eager to be imitators of the Lord, asking who may be wronged more, who may be defrauded, who may be rejected, so that no weed of the devil may be found among you, but you may remain in Jesus Christ in all purity and self-control, in flesh and in spirit.

last_rejected.source_quote: πρὸς τὰς ὀργὰς αὐτῶν ὑμεῖς πραεῖς
last_rejected.ruling: ὀργάς standardly means 'wrath/anger'; 'angers' is awkward but within normal range, not a major error

last_rejected.source_quote: πρὸς τὸ ἄγριον αὐτῶν ὑμεῖς ἥμεροι
last_rejected.why: ἥμεροι means 'gentle/mild', not 'tame' (which suggests domesticated animals)
last_rejected.ruling: ἥμεροι standardly means 'tame/gentle'; 'tame' is valid rendering, not misleading

last_rejected.quote: who was wronged more, who was defrauded more, who was rejected more?
last_rejected.source_quote: τίς πλέον ἀδικηθῇ, τίς ἀποστερηθῇ, τίς ἀθετηθῇ
last_rejected.why: Verbs are aorist passive subjunctive, not comparative; should be 'who was wronged, who was defrauded, who was rejected'
last_rejected.fix: who was wronged, who was defrauded, who was rejected
last_rejected.ruling: πλέον is comparative 'more'; English correctly renders it; verbs carry passive voice as translated

last_rejected.why: Adverbs mean 'in a fleshly/spiritual manner', not locative 'in flesh/spirit'
last_rejected.ruling: σαρκικῶς/πνευματικῶς as adverbs naturally rendered 'in flesh/spirit'; within normal range

last_rejected.quote: not eager to imitate them in return
last_rejected.why: Missing 'in return' (ἀντι- prefix); ἀντιμιμήσασθαι means 'imitate in return/retaliate'
last_rejected.fix: not eager to imitate them back in kind
last_rejected.ruling: English includes 'in return'; ἀντι- prefix is reflected; no omission present

polish.changed: Clarified the parallel structure in the second paragraph by making 'offer prayers' an action matching the other imperatives, and kept the rhetorical question about the Lord's suffering intact.

notes.why: 'Passible' (capable of suffering) vs 'passion' (suffering/death) are related but distinct; reader may miss Christological point.
notes.fix: Gloss 'passible' as 'capable of suffering' on first use.

notes.quote: who was wronged more, who was defrauded more, who was rejected more?
notes.why: Rhetorical question echoing Scripture or liturgy; source unclear.
notes.fix: Note: allusive rhetoric, possibly echoing Servant Songs or passion predictions.

notes.quote: as it is written, that the righteous one is his own accuser
notes.why: Cannot be placed in canonical scripture; possibly Proverbs 18:17 variant or non-canonical source.

notes.quote: Be gentle toward their angers, humble-minded toward their boasts, prayers toward their blasphemies
notes.why: Parallelism breaks: 'prayers' is a noun where an adjective or descriptor is expected, making the syntax garbled.
notes.fix: Render as 'prayerful toward their blasphemies' or 'offering prayer toward their blasphemies.'

polish.changed: Clarified 'angers' as 'outbursts of anger' and kept the rest of the translation faithful to the source while preserving the original paragraph breaks and all claims.

notes.quote: Be gentle toward their angers, humble-minded toward their boasts
notes.why: 'Angers' as plural noun is unusual; likely means 'outbursts of anger.'

polish.changed: Clarified the rhetorical questions as an allusion to Christ by adding 'asking' before them, and smoothed sentence rhythm while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: who was wronged more, who was defrauded, who was rejected?
notes.why: Rhetorical questions whose implied answer (Christ) is unstated; reader may miss allusion.
notes.fix: Add note: 'rhetorical questions referring to Christ's sufferings'.

polish.changed: Clarified the implied subject of the commands as the readers, smoothed the abrupt phrase 'obtain God' to 'attain God,' and restructured the list of contrasts into natural modern sentences while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: so that they may obtain God
notes.why: 'Obtain God' is abrupt; likely 'be found worthy of God' or 'attain God'.
notes.fix: 'that they may attain God' for consistency.

fixed: The speaker issue is not a translation error; the English already renders the source's indirect question. The suggested note is interpretive and not required by the source text.

problems.why: 'Tame' as an adjective applied to a person's disposition toward others is awkward; likely means 'gentle.'

fixed: Changed 'be tame toward their savagery' to 'be gentle toward their savagery' because the source ἥμεροι means 'gentle' or 'mild' in disposition, and 'tame' is awkward as an adjective applied to a person's manner toward others.

fixed: Changed 'obtain God' to 'attain God' to render ἵνα θεοῦ τύχωσιν more naturally; the Greek τύχωσιν means 'may attain/reach', and 'attain God' is the standard English idiom.
